note: Programs marked “Checked with agency” were confirmed on the agency’s or lender’s own site on that date; the rest come from current state guides and are re-checked against each agency on a rolling weekly basis. Lender grants apply only in the lender’s eligible areas. Always confirm amounts and eligibility with the program.

national.name: Chenoa Fund
national.notes: Forgivable after 36 on-time payments; a repayable version exists for higher incomes.

national.name: National Homebuyers Fund
national.notes: Grant or 3-year forgivable loan; first-time and repeat buyers.

national.name: Chase Homebuyer Grant
national.notes: Only for homes in eligible (mostly low- and moderate-income) census tracts, with a Chase DreaMaker, standard agency, FHA or VA purchase loan. Goes first to rate buydown and fees; can’t be used for the down payment on FHA. May be reported as income.

national.name: Bank of America Down Payment Grant
national.notes: Select markets only (260+ cities and counties). Used with Bank of America’s 3%-down mortgage; no homeownership in the past 3 years; income and loan limits apply. Never repaid.

national.name: America’s Home Grant®
national.notes: Select markets only. Covers nonrecurring closing costs (title, recording) or a permanent rate buydown — not the down payment. Stacks with the Down Payment Grant for up to $17,500.

programs.name: Closing Cost Assistance Program (CCAP)
programs.notes: Can go toward down payment, closing costs or principal reduction. The percentage depends on loan type and credit score (3% at 640–659 on FHA). Ask an AHFC-approved lender.

programs.name: HOME Opportunity Program (HOP)
programs.amountText: Closing-cost help for lower-income buyers — amount set by provider
programs.notes: Run through Cook Inlet Lending Center, NeighborWorks Alaska, Alaska Community Development Corp., Interior Regional Housing Authority and others.

programs.name: Step Up DPA
programs.notes: 10-year second mortgage paired with a 30-year fixed first mortgage from AHFA.

programs.name: Affordable Income Subsidy Grant
programs.notes: Closing costs only; HFA Advantage conventional loan only.

Huntsville.name: Down Payment Assistance
Huntsville.notes: 0% second, no payments; forgiven after 5 years in the home.

Mobile.name: Down Payment Assistance
Mobile.notes: Older source — confirm the program is still funded.

programs.name: Arkansas Dream Down Payment Initiative
programs.notes: Forgivable second mortgage; requires an ADFA first mortgage and homebuyer education.

programs.name: ADFA Down Payment Assistance
programs.notes: Second mortgage with a 10-year term; requires an ADFA StartSmart or Move-Up first mortgage.

AZ.name: Arizona
AZ.agency: Arizona IDA / Arizona Dept. of Housing

programs.name: HOME+PLUS DPA
programs.notes: Available year-round in every Arizona county; funding does not run out. 2026 income limits were raised — check the current limit with a Home Plus lender.

Maricopa County (incl. Phoenix).name: Home in Five Advantage
Maricopa County (incl. Phoenix).amountText: 5% of price (6% for educators, first responders, veterans)
Maricopa County (incl. Phoenix).notes: 0% forgivable second; forgiveness term not stated — confirm.

Maricopa County (incl. Phoenix).name: City of Phoenix DPA
Maricopa County (incl. Phoenix).amountText: Amount not published — call the city

Tucson / Pima County.name: City of Tucson DPA
Tucson / Pima County.amountText: Up to 20% of price, based on need
Tucson / Pima County.notes: Terms not stated — shown as deferred. $1,000 of your own funds required.

programs.name: MyHome Assistance
programs.amountText: Up to 3.5% of price/appraised value with CalHFA FHA; up to 3% with CalHFA Conventional, VA or USDA
programs.notes: Deferred-payment junior loan; must be paired with a CalHFA first mortgage. 640 min credit per CalHFA government-loan matrix (01/2026; 700 for DTI up to 50%); conventional pairing may require a higher score. Rate varies and is not published.

programs.name: Zero Interest Program (ZIP)
programs.amountText: 2% or 3% of first loan amount, closing costs and prepaids only
programs.notes: Used only with CalPLUS FHA first mortgage, in third-lien position behind MyHome. Repayment terms not stated on matrix; treated conservatively as deferred.

programs.name: Dream For All Shared Appreciation Loan
programs.amountText: Lesser of 20% of price/appraised value or $150,000
programs.incomeNote: Dream For All county income limits (e.g. ~$168k LA County, ~$309k Santa Clara County in 2026)
programs.notes: First-generation homebuyer required. Repay principal plus 20% of appreciation (15% if income at/below 80% AMI) on sale, transfer or payoff of first. Must use Dream For All Conventional first. 2026 application window closed March 16, 2026; vouchers issued by random selection; no future round dates announced.

City of Los Angeles.name: Low Income Purchase Assistance (LIPA)
City of Los Angeles.amountText: Up to $161,000 for down payment, closing costs and acquisition
City of Los Angeles.incomeNote: Low-income (~80% AMI; 2025 limit $121,150 for household of 4)
City of Los Angeles.notes: 0% deferred loan plus shared appreciation, due on sale/transfer/payoff or at 30 years. Funds reserved in limited rounds (last listed round March 4, 2026); call LAHD for current availability. First-time = no ownership in past 3 years. Eligible first-mortgage types not specified by LAHD.

City of Los Angeles.name: Moderate Income Purchase Assistance (MIPA)
City of Los Angeles.amountText: Up to $115,000 for down payment, closing costs and acquisition
City of Los Angeles.notes: 0% deferred loan plus shared appreciation, due on sale/transfer/payoff or 30-year balloon. Reserved in rounds (next listed Dec 16, 2026). Eligible first-mortgage types not specified by LAHD.

Los Angeles County.name: Home Ownership Program (HOP80 / HOP150)
Los Angeles County.amountText: Lesser of $100,000 or 20% of purchase price
Los Angeles County.incomeNote: HOP80 up to 80% AMI (price cap $700k); HOP150 up to 150% AMI (price cap $850k)
Los Angeles County.notes: 0% deferred shared-equity loan repaid with share of appreciation on sale/transfer/non-occupancy. Unincorporated LA County and participating cities only (not City of LA). First-come, first-served via participating lenders. Min credit and first-mortgage types not stated by LACDA.

City of San Diego.name: First-Time Homebuyer Program (Low-Income)
City of San Diego.amountText: Deferred loan up to 17% of price (max $125,000) plus forgivable closing-cost grant of 4% up to $10,000
City of San Diego.incomeNote: At or below 80% AMI; max price $883,025
City of San Diego.notes: 3% simple interest, payments deferred 30 years unless sold/no longer occupied. Requires fixed-rate first and 3% buyer down payment. SDHC intro text says up to 19% but program table says 17% (used here). Previous 22% figure applies to the County of San Diego program, not the City. No published min score ('good credit').

City of San Diego.name: First-Time Homebuyer Program (Middle-Income)
City of San Diego.notes: Loan at 4% simple interest deferred years 1-5, then amortizes over 120 months; the $10,000 grant is forgiven after 3 years of owner occupancy. ZIP codes beginning 921 only.

San Francisco.name: Downpayment Assistance Loan Program (DALP)
San Francisco.agency: SF Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development (MOHCD)
San Francisco.incomeNote: Up to ~200% AMI ($311,700 for household of 4)
San Francisco.notes: Silent second; repay principal plus share of appreciation on sale. Lottery-based: 2025 application period closed June 2, 2025; no 2026 round announced on sf.gov.

Santa Clara County / San Jose.name: Homebuyer Empowerment Loan Program (HELP)
Santa Clara County / San Jose.notes: Agency lists 'All Funds Allocated'. Repayment terms not published on page; treated conservatively as deferred. Replaces Empower Homebuyers SCC, which closed and sunset June 30, 2026.

programs.name: CHFA DPA Grant
programs.amountText: Lesser of 3% of first mortgage or $25,000
programs.notes: No repayment. Requires a CHFA first mortgage. First-generation buyers and borrowers with a permanent disability may get up to $25,000 regardless of loan size.

programs.name: CHFA Second Mortgage Loan
programs.amountText: Lesser of 4% of first mortgage or $25,000
programs.notes: Repayment deferred until payoff, sale, refinance, or the home is no longer your primary residence. First mortgage carries a higher rate than with the grant.

Colorado Springs / El Paso County.name: Turnkey Plus
Colorado Springs / El Paso County.notes: Half forgiven over 5 years; half deferred until payoff.

programs.name: Time To Own
programs.notes: 0% loan, no monthly payments, 10% forgiven each year. Requires a CHFA first mortgage and 3 years of Connecticut residency. Repeat buyers qualify in targeted areas.

Bridgeport.name: Down Payment Program
Bridgeport.notes: Forgiven over 5, 10 or 15 years depending on amount.

New Haven.name: Down Payment & Closing Cost Assistance
New Haven.notes: Fixed cash assistance added to an NH Housing mortgage, for down payment and closing costs. Forgiveness terms: confirm with NH Housing.

programs.name: DC Open Doors DPAL
programs.amountText: Covers the minimum required down payment
programs.notes: 0% loan, no monthly payments; due after 30 years or at sale, refinance or move-out. First-time and repeat buyers.

programs.name: Home Purchase Assistance Program (HPAP)
programs.amountText: Up to $202,000 gap financing + $4,000 closing costs
programs.notes: Under 80% AMI: deferred until sale, cash-out refinance or move-out. 80–110% MFI: payments deferred 5 years, then repaid over 40 years.

programs.name: Employer-Assisted Housing (DC employees)
programs.notes: DC government employees; first responders/educators get a different tier.

programs.name: DC4ME VA loan assistance
programs.notes: For qualified military-connected borrowers with a VA loan. Structure of the 3% not published — confirm with DCHFA.

programs.name: First State
programs.notes: 0% second mortgage, no monthly payment; due at refinance, sale, title transfer or move-out. Through DSHA Welcome Home (first-time) or Open Door (repeat buyers).

programs.name: Keys4You
programs.notes: 0% deferred second; Welcome Home (first-time) or Open Door (repeat buyers).

programs.name: Take5
programs.notes: 0% deferred second; Welcome Home (first-time buyers) only.

programs.name: Florida Assist (FL Assist)
programs.notes: Due in full on sale, transfer, refinance, satisfaction of first mortgage or non-occupancy. Requires a Florida Housing first mortgage; IRS first-time buyer definition (no ownership in 3 years).

programs.name: Florida Homeownership Loan Program (FL HLP) Second Mortgage
programs.amountText: $12,500 at 3%, fully amortizing over 30 years (monthly payment)
programs.notes: Payment counts in DTI; balance due on sale/refinance. Requires a Florida Housing first mortgage (agency page does not itemize loan types for HLP).

programs.name: 3%, 4% and 5% HFA Preferred / HFA Advantage PLUS Second Mortgage
programs.amountText: 3%, 4% or 5% of total first mortgage loan amount
programs.notes: Forgiven 20% per year over 5 years. Only with conventional HFA Preferred / HFA Advantage (TBA) first mortgages. pct shown is the minimum tier (3%).

programs.name: Florida Hometown Heroes Housing Program
programs.amountText: 5% of first mortgage loan amount, min $10,000, max $35,000; 0%, 30-year deferred, not forgivable
programs.notes: Full-time employees of Florida-based employers in health care, schools, first responders/public safety, courts, child care; active military/reserves/Guard; veterans. 2025-26 funds were fully committed Feb 2026; agency page now shows the HTH 2026 program (limits dated 7-13-26) and no exhaustion notice as of 2026-11-20. Funded in rounds, may close without notice. minCredit is Florida Housing's first-mortgage minimum.

Jacksonville.name: Head Start to Homeownership (H2H)
Jacksonville.agency: City of Jacksonville Housing & Community Development
Jacksonville.amountText: Up to $25,000 for down payment and closing costs
Jacksonville.incomeNote: At or below 80% of Duval County AMI
Jacksonville.notes: City page does not publish rate, term or forgiveness (contact program) - shown conservatively as deferred. Subject to funding limitations; home must pass HQS inspection. Loan types not specified.

Tampa.name: Dare to Own the Dream (DARE)
Tampa.agency: City of Tampa Housing & Community Development
Tampa.incomeNote: 50.01%-140% AMI; households under 50% AMI not eligible
Tampa.notes: 0% deferred silent second, forgiven after 20 years of occupancy. Purchase price cap $450,000; max back-end DTI 50%; buyer invests $2,000 ($1,000 own funds). City of Tampa limits only. City release 2026-10-28 says applications open.

Hillsborough County.name: Home Sweet Home Hillsborough
Hillsborough County.agency: Housing Finance Authority of Hillsborough County
Hillsborough County.amountText: Amount not published by HFA/administrator; 0% deferred 30-year second, never forgiven
Hillsborough County.notes: Countywide incl. Tampa. Repaid on sale/refinance/non-occupancy. First-time rule waived in Targeted Areas. Max price $450,000. Includes MCC. Page published by program administrator eHousingPlus, linked from hillsboroughcountyhfa.org.

Miami-Dade County.name: Homebuyer Down Payment Assistance Program
Miami-Dade County.amountText: Up to $35,000; 0% deferred, up to 30 years
Miami-Dade County.notes: Principal due on sale, transfer, refinance or death; County shares resale profit if sold within 6 years (100% yrs 1-3, 50% yrs 4-6). Fixed-rate first mortgage, CLTV max 105%, buyer contributes 1%. County residency required. Funding status not posted.

North Miami.name: First-Time Homebuyer Assistance (SHIP/HOME)
North Miami.notes: City calls it a forgivable deferred loan but does not publish the forgiveness schedule (affordability period 7 yrs SHIP / up to 15 yrs HOME) - shown conservatively as deferred. Open until funds are depleted. Max price $460,000 SHIP / $370,000 HOME.

Broward County.name: Homebuyer Purchase Assistance (HPA)
Broward County.amountText: Varies by participating city (county flyer cites up to $50,000-$120,000 in some communities); 0% deferred, 15-year term
Broward County.notes: Funds by city; June 2026 county flyer shows NO FUNDS for many communities - first-come, first-qualified. Buyer contributes 3% (not VA). Max price ~$679,324. Forgiveness not stated - shown as deferred.

Orlando.name: Orange County Homebuyer Down Payment Assistance
Orlando.notes: Closed to new applications (waitlist); anticipated reopening March 1, 2027, subject to state funding. Loan terms not published - shown conservatively as deferred.

Orlando.name: City of Orlando Down Payment Assistance
Orlando.agency: City of Orlando Housing & Community Development
Orlando.notes: Forgiven after 10 years if owner-occupied. Fixed-rate first mortgage from City-registered lender. City is not accepting new applications.

programs.name: Georgia Dream — Standard
programs.incomeNote: Income and price limits by county
programs.notes: 0% second mortgage, no monthly payment; repaid at sale or refinance. Homebuyer education required. Must use a Georgia Dream first mortgage.

programs.name: Georgia Dream — PEN / CHOICE
programs.incomeNote: Income and price limits by county
programs.notes: For protectors, educators, health-care workers and active military (PEN), or households with a member with a disability (CHOICE). 0% deferred second.

programs.name: Georgia Dream — Peach Plus
programs.amountText: Amount set by DCA — confirm with lender
programs.incomeNote: Higher limits: income to ~$237K, price to ~$725K
programs.notes: Open to repeat buyers. 0% deferred second.

City of Atlanta.name: ATL HomeNOW
City of Atlanta.notes: Down payment, closing costs and/or permanent rate reduction. Forgiven after 10 years as primary residence (Invest Atlanta page). Invest Atlanta also offers ATL Home Renovation Advantage ($10K), Perry Bolton and Vine City programs (area-specific).

City of Atlanta.name: Beltline Mortgage Assistance Program
City of Atlanta.amountText: Up to $20,000; up to $30,000 for legacy residents & public servants
City of Atlanta.incomeNote: 120% AMI (140% AMI tier available); Beltline TAD subareas 1, 2, 3, 8, 9, 10 only
City of Atlanta.notes: 0% soft second mortgage with 15-year affordability period; forgiveness terms not stated, so shown as deferred to be conservative. Up to $30,000 for civil servants and legacy residents. Max loan $400,000. 8-hour homebuyer education required.

City of Atlanta.name: Atlanta Housing Down Payment Assistance
City of Atlanta.amountText: Up to $20,000; up to $25,000 for public safety, healthcare, education, military/veterans and Housing Choice Voucher participants
City of Atlanta.notes: 0% community second; forgiven after 10 years of owner-occupancy with declining recapture (100% yrs 1-5, then 80/60/40/20%). First-time = no ownership in past 3 years. Fixed-rate conventional, FHA or VA first mortgage. Earlier $60K voucher-holder figure not found on Atlanta Housing site.

Fulton County (outside City of Atlanta).name: Fulton County Homeownership Program (HOP)
Fulton County (outside City of Atlanta).amountText: Up to $22,500 based on need (no % cap stated in 2026 guidelines)
Fulton County (outside City of Atlanta).incomeNote: At or below 80% AMI (4-person $94,250, eff. June 1, 2026); max price $347,000 existing / $367,000-$371,000 new
Fulton County (outside City of Atlanta).notes: 0% deferred second, no monthly payment; forgiven 20% per year over 5-year affordability period (HOP guidelines rev. June 2026). Down payment, closing costs and/or rate buydown. Guidelines list conventional/FHA/VA (USDA mentioned inconsistently). No set minimum credit score. HOME-funded, first come first ready until funds run out.

Gwinnett County.name: Homestretch Down Payment Assistance
Gwinnett County.notes: 0% no-payment soft second, forgiven 20% per year over 5-year affordability period. Fixed-rate FHA, VA or conventional only (no 203k). Single-family, townhome or condo. First-time = no ownership in 3 years.

DeKalb County.name: DeKalb HomeStart
DeKalb County.amountText: Amount not yet published by DeKalb County (news reports cited ~$20,000)
DeKalb County.notes: Announced July 14, 2026 as part of the $155M housing investment bond: down payment, closing cost and rate buydown help, enhanced for first responders/public servants. No application or terms published on county site yet; type shown as deferred to be conservative.

DeKalb County.name: WE DeKalb
DeKalb County.amountText: 1%-3% grant of loan amount (program not currently available)
DeKalb County.notes: eHousingPlus program page (Aug 2026): 'as previously offered, is not currently available' and under strategic review. Non-repayable grant when offered.

Savannah.name: DreamMaker Home Purchase Assistance
Savannah.amountText: Up to $30,000 (up to $50,000 for city-partnered homes)
Savannah.incomeNote: Income limits apply; city limits only
Savannah.notes: 2% interest, 30-year deferred-payment loan (city page); up to $50,000 for city-partnered housing. Forgiveness not stated. Year-round while funds remain. Credit and loan-type rules not stated on city page.

Augusta-Richmond County.name: Homeownership Assistance Program
Augusta-Richmond County.amountText: Up to $10,000 toward down payment and closing costs
Augusta-Richmond County.notes: Augusta HCD lists up to $10,000 (previously shown as $5,000); repayment/forgiveness terms not stated, so shown as deferred to be conservative. Subject to available funding; rolling review. City/RCSO employees may get up to $15,000 (Officer Next Door).

Columbus.name: Sweet Home Columbus
Columbus.incomeNote: At or below 80% AMI (4-person $67,750); max price ~$252,000 (HOME limit)
Columbus.notes: 0% deferred loan (city page); 2026 policy (eff. July 1, 2026) describes pro-rated forgiveness over 5 yrs (<$25K) or 10 yrs ($25K+), while the web page says residency up to 15 years, so shown as deferred to be conservative. Fixed-rate 30-year first mortgage only. 8-hour counseling required. First-time = no ownership in 3 years.

Cobb County.name: Cobb County My Home DPA
Cobb County.agency: Housing Authority of Cobb County (administered by eHousingPlus)
Cobb County.amountText: 1% or 2% of loan amount grant (+$10,000 for Cobb County employees; $10K-$15K for eligible City of Marietta employees)
Cobb County.incomeNote: Income limits apply (approx. $90,800 at 80% AMI / $159,880 higher tier per Aug 2025 guide)
Cobb County.notes: Non-repayable grant paired with program 30-year fixed first mortgage; no second lien. No first-time buyer requirement. Min FICO 640 (VA/Freddie HFA Advantage), 660 FHA. Terms from program guide rev. 08-27-25.

Clayton County.name: Clayton County Down Payment Assistance Program
Clayton County.agency: Clayton County Office of Grants Administration (HUD)
Clayton County.amountText: Up to $7,500; up to $10,000 for veterans/spouses, county employees, law enforcement, first responders, healthcare and education workers
Clayton County.incomeNote: At or below 80% AMI; max purchase price $270,000
Clayton County.notes: Interest-free soft second, fully forgiven after 5 or 10 years of occupancy depending on amount. Lender sets credit minimum. No condos or mobile homes; $1,000 buyer contribution; 8-hour HUD education. Eligible first-mortgage types not listed (all shown). First-time = no ownership in 3 years.

programs.name: Military Homeownership Assistance
programs.notes: Funds remain for fiscal 2027 (about $1.1 million as of Nov 2, 2026). For eligible service members and veterans.

Davenport.name: First-Time Home Buyer Grant
Davenport.amountText: Half your down payment + closing costs, up to $10,000

programs.name: Idaho Housing Second Mortgage
programs.amountText: Up to 7% of price (8% on some products)
programs.notes: Fixed rate 2% above your first mortgage, repaid over 15 years. You contribute at least $500 (0.5% on some products). Finally Home!® education required.

programs.name: Idaho Housing Forgivable Loan
programs.notes: Raises the first-mortgage rate slightly.

programs.name: IHDA Access Forgivable
programs.incomeNote: IHDA income and purchase price limits apply (see ihdamortgage.org/limits)
programs.notes: Forgiven monthly over 10 years. Paired with IHDA 30-yr fixed first mortgage; conventional = Fannie HFA Preferred / Freddie HFA Advantage. Buyer contribution greater of $1,000 or 1%; max DTI 50%; homebuyer counseling required. IHDA notes funding can change at any time.

programs.name: IHDA Access Deferred
programs.incomeNote: IHDA income and purchase price limits apply (see ihdamortgage.org/limits)
programs.notes: Interest-free, deferred for the life of the first mortgage; repaid on sale, refinance or payoff. Buyer contribution greater of $1,000 or 1%; max DTI 50%; counseling required.

programs.name: IHDA Access Repayable
programs.incomeNote: IHDA income and purchase price limits apply (see ihdamortgage.org/limits)
programs.notes: Zero-interest second loan repaid in monthly installments over 10 years. Buyer contribution greater of $1,000 or 1%; max DTI 50%; counseling required.

programs.name: IHDA Access Home
programs.incomeNote: IHDA income and purchase price limits apply (see ihdamortgage.org/limits)
programs.notes: Interest-free, deferred for life of the mortgage; repaid on sale, refinance or payoff. First-time buyers only, except eligible veterans (COE/DD214) or purchases in IHDA targeted areas. Buyer contribution greater of $1,000 or 1%; max DTI 50%.

programs.name: IHDA Opening Doors
programs.incomeNote: IHDA income and purchase price limits apply (see ihdamortgage.org/limits)
programs.notes: Forgiven monthly over 5 years; unforgiven balance repaid if sold/refinanced earlier. First-time and repeat buyers. Listed as 'Now Open' on ihdamortgage.org.

Aurora.name: Choose Aurora Homebuyer Assistance
Aurora.amountText: $20,000 0% deferred loan, plus $5,000 closing-cost grant for households ≤80% AMI (up to $2,000 small-repairs grant may also apply)
Aurora.incomeNote: ≤120% AMI (e.g. $145,800 for household of 4); $5,000 grant only ≤80% AMI
Aurora.notes: Deferred soft second repaid on sale, title change, cash-out refi or end of owner occupancy; no forgiveness stated. Max $25,000 assumes ≤80% AMI ($20,000 for 81–120% AMI); city page cites up to $27,000 incl. repair grant. Amount set by city staff based on need. First-time rule, credit score and loan types not stated by city. Funding availability not stated; HUD counseling required.

Joliet.name: Joliet Down Payment Assistance Program
Joliet.amountText: Minimum $1,000; maximum up to 20% of purchase price (no dollar cap published)
Joliet.notes: City page states the program is not currently taking applications. 0% deferred loan described as forgivable, but forgiveness period is not published, so typed conservatively as deferred. Buyer must contribute $2,500. Replaces prior 'Illinois Assist' listing, which is not a City of Joliet program.

Chicago.name: HomeGrown Purchase Assistance Grant
Chicago.agency: City of Chicago Dept. of Housing (administered by NLS and TRP Lending)
Chicago.amountText: Up to $70,000 (Zone A) or $50,000 (Zone B), capped at 25% of purchase price
Chicago.incomeNote: Zone A ≤120% AMI; Zone B ≤150% AMI
Chicago.notes: Forgiven 1/60 per month over 5 years of owner occupancy. Buyer cannot own any other home at purchase. Fixed-rate first mortgage required; max back-end DTI 38%; no 3–4 unit buildings. First-come, first-served; waitlist possible if funds run out. Terms confirmed on administrator NHS Chicago/NLS page (updated Jul 2026); chicago.gov page could not be fetched. Min credit not published.

Cook County.name: Cook County Down Payment Assistance Program
Cook County.agency: Cook County Bureau of Economic Development
Cook County.amountText: 5% of first loan amount, up to $25,000
Cook County.incomeNote: ≤120% AMI ($145,800 for household of 4); no income limit in Disproportionately Impacted Areas / Qualified Census Tracts
Cook County.notes: Phase III ($2M, ~100 buyers) launched Jul 20, 2026 through participating lenders; funds limited and may run out. Forgivable second over 5 years; usable for down payment, closing costs or rate buydown. First-time and repeat buyers per county page (first-timers need HUD counseling). Formerly listed here as 'Home Advantage'.

Kane County.name: Kane County First-Time Homebuyer Loan Program
Kane County.agency: Kane County Office of Community Reinvestment
Kane County.amountText: Up to $10,000 (additional $10,000 possible in St. Charles)
Kane County.incomeNote: Federal HOME income limits (figures not published on page)
Kane County.notes: 0% deferred loan repaid on sale, transfer or end of principal residence. Excludes City of Aurora (see Aurora) and Hampshire, Huntley, Hoffman Estates, Montgomery; includes Elgin. Must live/work in area 1 yr, 1% down, HUD counseling. Funding availability not stated.

Rockford.name: Rockford Homebuyer Assistance Program
Rockford.notes: City page states the program is closed for applications. 5-year forgivable loan (occupancy described as ~6 years); unoccupied detached single-family homes within city limits only.

programs.name: Next Home
programs.notes: Paired with a 30-year fixed FHA or conventional loan; capped at appraised value.

Evansville.name: Homebuyer Program
Evansville.notes: Forgiven after 5, 10 or 15 years depending on amount.

programs.name: First-Time Homebuyer Program
programs.incomeNote: ≤80% AMI; not in Topeka, Lawrence, Wichita, KCK or Johnson County

Wichita.name: HOMEownership 80
Wichita.amountText: Up to 20% of price + $2,000 closing costs
Wichita.notes: Half forgiven after 5 or 10 years depending on amount.

Louisville Metro.name: Down Payment Assistance
Louisville Metro.notes: 0% loan; half forgivable over time, rest due at sale or refinance.

programs.name: MRB Home grant
programs.notes: Below-market rate. LHC is moving programs to its HomeStart lineup — confirm this one is still offered.

programs.name: HomeStart Advantage (Keys for Service)
programs.notes: For full-time law enforcement, firefighters, paramedics and certified teachers. Forgivable assistance.

programs.name: HomeStart Assist
programs.notes: 0% forgivable second mortgage with a 30-year fixed first mortgage at about market rate. First-time and repeat buyers.

programs.name: HomeStart Plus (disaster-affected areas)
programs.notes: Enhanced assistance for homes in designated disaster-affected parishes. Amount from earlier Resilience Soft Second terms — confirm with LHC.

programs.name: MassHousing DPA Option 1
programs.notes: 0% interest, deferred until sale, refinance or first-mortgage payoff. Income-eligible first-time buyers.

programs.name: MassHousing DPA Option 2
programs.notes: 2% fixed, repaid over 15 years. A third option is $25,000 at 3% over 15 years.

programs.name: 1st Time Advantage 6000
programs.notes: 0% deferred second loan for down payment and closing costs, with an MMP first mortgage.

programs.name: First Homes for First Responders and Teachers
programs.notes: Launched Sept 2026. First mortgage rate 0.50% below MMP 1st Time Advantage 5%. At least one borrower must work in Maryland as an EMT, firefighter, police officer or teacher.

programs.name: House Keys 4 Employees (State of Maryland staff)
programs.amountText: Extra $2,500 on top of the $6,000 DPA ($8,500 total)
programs.notes: Active State of Maryland employees (permanent or contractual). 0% deferred; needs a 1st Time Advantage 6000 or Flex 6000 loan and homebuyer education.

Baltimore City.name: Buying Into Baltimore
Baltimore City.notes: 20 winners per year; no income limit.

Montgomery County.name: Montgomery Homeownership Program
Montgomery County.notes: 0% deferred second with an MMP first mortgage. Reservations were limited in spring 2026; expected to fully reopen in fiscal 2027.

Howard County.name: Settlement Downpayment Loan Program
Howard County.notes: Deferred; interest 2 points below your first mortgage.

Prince George's County.name: Pathway to Purchase
Prince George's County.notes: County down payment and closing cost assistance, combined with a Maryland Mortgage Program first mortgage.

programs.name: Advantage Down Payment
programs.notes: Grant, no second mortgage and no repayment. Needs a MaineHousing First Home Loan, a hoMEworks homebuyer class, and a 1% borrower contribution (may be a gift).

programs.name: Multi-Unit Advantage
programs.notes: 1–4 unit properties.

programs.name: Salute ME / Salute Home Again
programs.notes: For active duty, veterans and retired military. First-time buyer rule waived for veterans who owned before. 1% borrower contribution required.

programs.name: MI 10K DPA
programs.incomeNote: 236 eligible ZIP codes only; price cap
programs.notes: Available statewide; homebuyer education class required. Paired with an MSHDA first mortgage.

Detroit.name: Detroit Down Payment Assistance
Detroit.notes: Terms not stated — shown as deferred.

Detroit.name: National Faith DPA
Detroit.notes: Detroit / Wayne County; existing homes only.

Warren.name: Direct Homebuyer Assistance
Warren.amountText: Half your down payment + $2,500 closing, max $14,000

programs.name: Monthly Payment Loan
programs.notes: Same rate as the first mortgage, repaid over 10 years. Works with Start Up (first-time) and Step Up (repeat) loans; no separate income limit.

programs.name: Deferred Payment Loan
programs.notes: 0% balloon loan due at sale, refinance, move-out or first-mortgage payoff. Start Up (first-time buyers) only.

programs.name: Deferred Payment Loan Plus
programs.notes: 0% deferred; for Start Up borrowers who meet the DPL Plus targeting criteria.

programs.name: First Place CashAssistance
programs.notes: 0% forgivable second; starts reducing by 1/60 a month after year 5, gone at year 10. First-time buyers or qualified veterans; must repay if you sell or refinance within 10 years.

programs.name: Next Step CashAssistance
programs.notes: First-time and repeat buyers above First Place income limits. 0% forgivable second over 10 years; up to 50% DTI.

programs.name: Smart7
programs.notes: 0% second, due at sale, refinance, move-out or first-mortgage payoff. Purchase price ≤ $398,310.

programs.name: Easy8
programs.notes: 0% second, due at sale, refinance, move-out or first-mortgage payoff. Homebuyer education required.

programs.name: Trusty10
programs.notes: 2% second mortgage repaid over 15 years. First-time rule waived in target areas and for veterans. Mississippi REALTORS® adds $2,000 more ("Trusty 10 Plus 2") while funds last.

programs.name: Housing Assistance for Teachers
programs.notes: Certified public school teachers in eligible areas.

programs.name: Home4All
programs.notes: HOME-funded; homebuyer education through a HUD-approved counselor required. Assistance can’t exceed 50% of the price. Repayment terms: confirm with MHC (shown as deferred).

programs.name: NC Home Advantage DPA
programs.notes: 0% deferred second, forgiven 20% a year in years 11–15. First-time and move-up buyers. Repay only if you sell, refinance or transfer before year 15.

programs.name: NC 1st Home Advantage Down Payment
programs.notes: 0% deferred second, forgiven 20% a year in years 11–15. First-time buyers, military veterans, or homes in targeted census tracts. Can’t be combined with the 3% option.

programs.name: Down Payment & Closing Cost Assistance
programs.notes: Fixed cash assistance added to an NH Housing mortgage, for down payment and closing costs. Forgiveness terms: confirm with NH Housing.

programs.name: 1stGenHomeNH
programs.notes: For first-generation buyers, on top of the standard NH Housing assistance. Terms: confirm with NH Housing (shown as deferred).

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.agency: NJ Housing and Mortgage Finance Agency (NJHMFA)

programs.name: First Generation DPA
programs.notes: For first-generation buyers (no parent or spouse has owned a home). Combined with the NJHMFA DPA for up to $22,000 total.

programs.name: FIRSTDown
programs.notes: Low fixed-rate second mortgage with 10-, 15- or 30-year terms; must be paired with a FirstHome loan. All Housing New Mexico assistance combined is capped at $35,000.

programs.name: FirstDown Plus
programs.notes: 0% loan, no payments, forgiven in year 11; down payment only (not closing costs). Requires a FirstHome loan; funds first come, first served.

programs.name: HOMENow
programs.notes: 0% second with a 10-year affordability period; paired with a FirstHome loan. Funds limited, first come first served.

programs.name: Home Is Possible for First-Time Homebuyers
programs.notes: 0% second mortgage, no payments, 30-year note, not forgiven. Rate is a bit higher with the 4% option. Homebuyer education required.

programs.name: Home First
programs.notes: Down payment only (not closing costs). Forgiven after 3 years in the home. 6 months Nevada residency and homebuyer education required.

programs.name: Home Is Possible
programs.notes: No first-time-buyer requirement. Structure of the assistance: confirm with a HIP lender (shown as deferred).

NY.name: New York
NY.agency: State of New York Mortgage Agency (SONYMA)

programs.name: SONYMA Down Payment Assistance Loan (DPAL)
programs.amountText: Greater of $3,000 or 3% of price, capped at $15,000 (min $1,000; cannot exceed actual down payment/closing costs)
programs.notes: 0% second lien, no payments, forgiven after 10 years (pro-rated 1/120 per month if sold/refinanced earlier). Only with a SONYMA first mortgage; first-mortgage rate is 0.40% higher with DPAL (except Graduate to Homeownership, Homes for Veterans, ENERGY STAR). Buyer must contribute 1% (3% co-ops/3-4 family). SONYMA programs require first-time buyers except veterans/Target Areas. Min credit score not published on HCR site; loan insurance types not stated on DPAL page.

programs.name: SONYMA DPAL Plus 2026
programs.amountText: Up to $30,000 (down payment, closing costs, single-premium MI)
programs.notes: Launched July 1, 2026; statewide via participating SONYMA lenders, first-come first-served until funds run out. HCR page does not publish forgiveness/repayment terms (refers to a separate term sheet), so typed conservatively as deferred. Must be applied after any other subsidies/grants.

programs.name: SONYMA Repayable Second Lien (RSL)
programs.amountText: Up to 5% of net purchase price (min $3,000; cannot exceed actual down payment/closing costs)
programs.notes: 0% interest, no monthly payments; repaid on sale, refinance or payoff of the SONYMA first mortgage. Alternative to DPAL (larger % but never forgiven). First-mortgage rate +0.40% (with same exceptions as DPAL).

programs.name: SONYMA Conventional Plus / FHA Plus
programs.amountText: Down payment & closing cost assistance included — amount not published on HCR page
programs.notes: 30-year fixed Conventional or FHA first mortgage bundled with SONYMA DPA; open to first-time and returning buyers. HCR page gives no DPA amount or forgiveness terms, so typed conservatively as deferred with amount unknown.

New York City.name: HomeFirst Down Payment Assistance
New York City.notes: Forgivable loan with owner-occupancy period of 10 years if ≤$40,000, 15 years if over $40,000 (City-funded loans: 15 years regardless). Buyer must contribute 3% of price; HPD-approved homebuyer education required; 1-4 family, condo or co-op in the five boroughs; price at or below 95% of HUD limits.

Buffalo.name: City of Buffalo Down Payment & Closing Cost Assistance (via Belmont)
Buffalo.agency: City of Buffalo / Belmont Housing Resources for WNY
Buffalo.amountText: Up to $15,000 for down payment and closing costs
Buffalo.notes: Listed on Belmont's First Time Homebuyer Programs page; apply through a Belmont counselor (716-884-7791). Structure, income limits and funding status not published, so typed conservatively as deferred.

Rochester.name: Home Purchase Assistance Program (HPAP)
Rochester.notes: City calls it a grant but requires 5 years of owner-occupancy, so modeled as forgivable over 5 years. 1-4 family homes in City of Rochester; buyer contributes $1,500; pre/post-purchase training required. First mortgage (Conventional, FHA, VA or SONYMA) of at least $25,000.

Westchester County.name: Westchester County Home Ownership Initiative
Westchester County.notes: All or part repayable if owner moves, sells or violates terms within the required occupancy period (period not legible on county page) — typed conservatively as deferred. House, condo or co-op in Westchester County; Yonkers eligibility not confirmed on the page. Funding status not stated.

Syracuse.name: Home HeadQuarters Closing Cost Assistance
Syracuse.incomeNote: 3% rate if <80% HUD median; up to 6% otherwise
Syracuse.notes: Amortizing loan repaid over 5 years at up to 6% simple interest (3% for <80% median income). Available anywhere in NY State except NYC; buyer must put $500 of own funds and complete homebuyer education.

Ithaca / Tompkins region.name: INHS Down Payment Assistance
Ithaca / Tompkins region.notes: For purchases in Cayuga, Chemung, Cortland, Schuyler, Seneca, Tioga or Tompkins counties. Structure not stated (typed conservatively as deferred); availability depends on grant funding.

programs.name: OHFA Down Payment Assistance
programs.notes: Formerly "Your Choice!". Forgiven after 7 years; repay it all if you sell sooner. FHA needs 650 credit; VA and USDA 640.

programs.name: Grants for Grads
programs.notes: For first-time buyers who earned a degree within the last 18 months; also a lower interest rate. Forgiven after 5 years if you stay in Ohio.

programs.name: OHFA Homebuyer DPA
programs.notes: First-time and repeat buyers, all 77 counties; FHA, HUD-184, USDA, VA or conventional. Secured by a lien. Special rates for school employees, first responders and state employees.

programs.name: Flex Lending DPA
programs.notes: FirstHome (first-time) or NextStep (anyone income-eligible). Can cover 100% of cash to close and stack with other DPA. Above 80% AMI it’s a 30-year amortizing second at the first-mortgage rate + 1%.

programs.name: Keystone Advantage Assistance Loan
programs.amountText: Lesser of 4% of price/appraised value or $6,000 ($8,000 for participating Employer Assisted Housing employees)
programs.incomeNote: PHFA first-mortgage income limits apply; liquid assets max $50,000 after closing
programs.notes: 0% second mortgage repaid monthly over 10 years. Requires a PHFA first mortgage (Keystone Home, Keystone Government or HFA Preferred). Covers only minimum required down payment/closing costs; minimum $500. Cannot be combined with other PHFA DPA (except Access Modification).

programs.name: Keystone Forgivable in Ten Years (K-FIT)
programs.amountText: 5% of the lesser of price or appraised value, no dollar cap
programs.incomeNote: PHFA first-mortgage income limits apply; liquid assets max $50,000 after closing
programs.notes: Forgiven 10% per year over 10 years; prorated repayment on sale, transfer or non-owner occupancy. Only with Keystone Home Loan (or Keystone Flex). Covers only minimum required down payment/closing costs.

programs.name: Keystone Due At Time of Expiration (K-DATE)
programs.amountText: 8% of the lesser of price or appraised value for first mortgages up to $150,000 (subject to availability); 5% for first mortgages over $150,000; no dollar cap
programs.incomeNote: PHFA first-mortgage income limits apply; liquid assets max $50,000 after closing
programs.notes: Launched May 2026. 0% 30-year second mortgage, no monthly payments; due in full on sale, refinance or first-mortgage payoff. pct shows the 5% tier for loans over $150k; 8% tier for smaller loans. Keystone Home Loan / Keystone Flex only.

programs.name: HOMEstead DPA
programs.incomeNote: County-specific HOMEstead income and purchase price limits; not available in major cities/7 counties with their own HUD allocation
programs.notes: PHFA paused HOMEstead until further notice for reservations on or after Aug 7, 2026 (Q3 2026 program update). Was a 0% second forgiven 20%/yr over 5 years with Keystone Home Loan.

programs.name: Access Downpayment & Closing Cost Assistance (disability)
programs.incomeNote: Household income at or below 80% of statewide median family income
programs.notes: Buyer or household member with a disability; must also use the Access Home Modification Loan. 0% interest, no monthly payment; repaid on sale, transfer or non-owner occupancy. Not combinable with other PHFA DPA.

programs.name: PHFA Grant
programs.notes: Only with HFA Preferred (Lo MI) conventional first mortgage; can be combined with Keystone Advantage Assistance.

Philadelphia.name: Philly First Home
Philadelphia.incomeNote: Household income limits apply (e.g. $122,700 for a household of 4)
Philadelphia.notes: Described as a grant, but must be repaid if the buyer moves or refinances before living in the home 15 years (city page does not describe proration). First-time = no ownership in 3 years. City-funded counseling required before signing agreement of sale. Single-family or duplex; no condos. Offered while funding is available. Loan types not specified by the city.

Pittsburgh.name: Down Payment and Closing Cost Assistance Program
Pittsburgh.amountText: Up to $7,500 (under 80% AMI) or up to $5,000 (80-115% AMI)
Pittsburgh.notes: 0% deferred loan, not a grant: 5-year term (<80% AMI) or 10-year (80-115% AMI), no payments if residency met; URA does not state forgiveness explicitly, so typed conservatively as deferred. City of Pittsburgh only; HUD-certified homebuyer course; max $20,000 liquid assets after closing; 2% closing fee; apply 21 business days before closing.

Allegheny County (outside Pittsburgh).name: 1st Home Allegheny
Allegheny County (outside Pittsburgh).agency: Allegheny County Economic Development / Residential Finance Authority
Allegheny County (outside Pittsburgh).notes: Forgivable subordinate loan, 6-year term (county page does not detail forgiveness schedule). Excludes City of Pittsburgh. No home owned in last 3 years; buyer contributes $1,000 or 1% of price; assets under $40,000; 2 months reserves; HUD-certified education. Limited funding ($2.6M); page says accepting applications.

Bethlehem.name: Bethlehem Homebuyer Assistance Program (BHAP)
Bethlehem.agency: City of Bethlehem / Community Action Lehigh Valley
Bethlehem.amountText: Up to 10% of the financing plus closing costs; no dollar cap stated
Bethlehem.notes: 0% deferred loan forgiven gradually over 10 years; prorated repayment if not occupied 10 years. Buyer contributes $1,275 and completes counseling. City page gives no current open/closed status; confirm with CACLV. Allentown city has no direct homebuyer DPA program (per its Grants Dept).

programs.name: Statewide DPA Grant
programs.notes: The ARPA-funded $17,500 grant ($30M) helped about 1,600 buyers and is no longer listed among RIHousing’s current programs. Ask RIHousing whether new funding is coming.

programs.name: 15kDPA
programs.notes: 0% loan, no monthly payments; due when you sell, refinance or move out. Needs a RIHousing first mortgage and homebuyer education.

programs.name: Extra Assistance
programs.notes: Repayable second at the same rate as your RIHousing first mortgage. Homebuyer education required.

programs.name: FirstGenHomeRI
programs.notes: Pilot with limited funds. First-generation buyers currently living in Central Falls, East Providence, Pawtucket, Woonsocket, Providence (not 02906) or one Newport tract. Forgiven after 5 years.

programs.name: Palmetto Home Advantage
programs.notes: Forgivable, no monthly payment. First-time, move-up and repeat buyers in all 46 counties; no price limit.

programs.name: Palmetto Heroes
programs.notes: For teachers, law enforcement, firefighters, EMS, nurses, correctional officers, veterans, active duty and National Guard. Funded in yearly rounds — check whether this year’s round is open.

programs.name: Great Choice — Deferred
programs.notes: 0% Great Choice Plus second, forgiven after 10 years; due in full if you sell or refinance sooner. Homebuyer education required.

programs.name: Great Choice — Amortizing
programs.notes: 30-year amortizing second at the same rate as the first mortgage.

programs.name: Great Choice — new construction
programs.notes: Higher assistance for newly built homes from participating builders; repaid over 30 years.

programs.name: Homeownership for Heroes
programs.notes: Reduced Great Choice rate for military, veterans and other eligible service members; first-time rule waived statewide for qualified military and veterans.

Chattanooga.name: CNE second loan
Chattanooga.notes: Rate 0.5 points below your first mortgage.

TX.name: Texas
TX.agency: TDHCA / Texas State Affordable Housing Corp. (TSAHC)

programs.name: My First Texas Home
programs.incomeNote: Income and purchase-price limits by county
programs.notes: 0% second lien, no payments, due on sale/refinance/payoff of first lien. A 3-year forgivable 2nd-lien option also exists. First-time = no ownership in 3 yrs; exceptions in targeted areas and for qualified veterans. Homebuyer education required. Program matrix dated 2/3/2025.

programs.name: My Choice Texas Home
programs.incomeNote: Income and purchase-price limits by county; separate options ≤80% AMI and >80% AMI
programs.notes: 0% second lien, no payments, due on sale/refinance/payoff of first lien. A 3-year forgivable 2nd-lien option also exists. Conventional = Fannie HFA Preferred / Freddie HFA Advantage. Homebuyer education required.

programs.name: Home Sweet Texas Home Loan Program
programs.amountText: Up to 5% of loan (grant or 3-year forgivable second lien)
programs.incomeNote: Low/moderate income limits by county (up to ~80% / 150–170% AMI)
programs.notes: Offered as either a non-repayable grant or a second lien forgiven after 3 years; modeled conservatively as forgivable. Min credit 620 government / 640 conventional. Specific government loan types not named on the page. Purchase-price limits by county.

programs.name: Homes for Texas Heroes Home Loan Program
programs.amountText: Up to 5% of loan (grant or 3-year forgivable second lien)
programs.incomeNote: Income limits by county (up to ~80% / 150–170% AMI)
programs.notes: For teachers/K-12 staff, police, firefighters, EMS, corrections officers, nursing/allied health faculty and veterans. Grant or 3-yr forgivable option; modeled conservatively as forgivable. Min credit 620 government / 640 conventional.

Houston.name: Homebuyer Assistance Program (HAP)
Houston.incomeNote: ≤80% AMI (CDBG); up to 120% AMI for TIRZ-funded
Houston.notes: Closed to new applications: program funds exhausted (Nov 2026). 0% forgivable junior lien: ≤$50,000 forgiven over 5 yrs, $50,000.01–$75,000 over 8 yrs (Guidelines v8.0, eff. 6/23/2026). No minimum credit score. Home must be in City of Houston.

Harris County.name: Harris County Downpayment Assistance Program (DAP)
Harris County.incomeNote: Income-qualified; price ≤$285,000 existing / $296,000 new; unincorporated Harris County only
Harris County.notes: At capacity: currently accepting only Hurricane Beryl/Derecho-affected applicants. Silent second mortgage with 5-yr (<$25k) or 10-yr ($25k–$40k) affordability period; forgiveness not stated explicitly, so modeled as deferred. Loan types not listed by the county.

San Antonio.name: Homeownership Incentive Program (HIP 80)
San Antonio.notes: 0% no-payment second lien. Forgiven over 5 years if ≤$15,000, 10 years if more. First lien must be Conventional, FHA or VA. Home within San Antonio city limits.

San Antonio.name: Homeownership Incentive Program (HIP 120)
San Antonio.notes: 0% no-payment second lien: 75% forgiven over 10 years, 25% is perpetual (repaid on sale/refinance), so modeled as deferred. First-time rule and loan types not stated on the HIP page; loan types assumed same as HIP 80.

Dallas.name: Dallas Homebuyer Assistance Program (DHAP)
Dallas.agency: City of Dallas (administered by BCL of Texas)
Dallas.amountText: Up to $50,000; up to $60,000 in High Opportunity Areas
Dallas.notes: Administered by BCL of Texas since May 1, 2026. 0% forgivable deferred second lien prorated annually over the affordability term (term length not published). Funding first-come, first-served. Anti-Displacement DHAP (50–120% AMI, 10-yr Dallas residents) up to $50,000; Targeted Occupations DHAP funds fully spent. First-time rule, min credit and loan types not stated on agency pages.

Austin.name: Down Payment Assistance
Austin.agency: City of Austin Housing / Austin Housing Finance Corp.
Austin.notes: Standard DPA (≤$14,999) is a 0% loan forgiven after 5 years. Shared-equity DPA ($15k–$40k) is forgiven after 10 years but the City's shared-equity interest remains for 30 years, so modeled as deferred. No program credit minimum (lenders may set one). Loan types not specified by the City. Home in Austin full-purpose city limits.

Fort Worth.name: Homebuyer Assistance Program (HAP)
Fort Worth.agency: City of Fort Worth Neighborhood Services
Fort Worth.amountText: Up to $25,000 (deferred loan plus closing costs up to 3% of loan)
Fort Worth.notes: ≤$14,999 forgiven after 5 years; amounts up to $25,000 require 10 years residency. First mortgage must be 30-yr fixed from a city-approved lender; specific loan types not listed. Subject to funding availability (guidelines rev. 4/15/2026).

Corpus Christi.name: Homebuyer Assistance Program
Corpus Christi.notes: Not verified 2026-11-20: the former cctexas.com program page now redirects to the new city homepage and no current program page was found. Confirm with City of Corpus Christi before relying on these figures.

programs.name: UHC Down Payment Assistance
programs.amountText: Covers the minimum down payment (up to ~6%)
programs.notes: Traditional option: 30-year amortizing second at 1% above the first-mortgage rate. UHC now also offers a deferred-payment DPA. First-time and repeat buyers.

programs.name: First-Time Homebuyer New Construction
programs.notes: 0% loan from state funds (SB 240). Use for down payment, closing costs or a permanent rate buydown. 12 months Utah residency required; can stack with the UHC DPA second.

programs.name: First-Time Homebuyer Veterans Grant
programs.notes: State grant for veterans buying in Utah; funds appropriated by the Legislature and limited.

programs.name: Down Payment Assistance Grant
programs.notes: A true gift, never repaid. Down payment only. First-time buyers unless in a targeted area. Can’t be combined with the Plus Second or Closing Cost grant.

programs.name: Closing Cost Assistance Grant
programs.notes: Grant, never repaid, for buyers using a VA or USDA (RHS) loan.

programs.name: Virginia Housing Plus Second
programs.amountText: Covers the down payment (plus some closing costs)
programs.notes: 30-year fixed second mortgage, no prepayment penalty. First-time or repeat buyers, including those over the grant income limits.

programs.name: ASSIST
programs.notes: 0% deferred loan, not forgiven — repaid at sale, refinance or payoff. True first-time buyers with under $20,000 in combined liquid assets; only with VHFA MOVE.

programs.name: NeighborWorks of Western VT DPA
programs.notes: Rate 2 points above your mortgage.

programs.name: First Generation Homebuyer Grant
programs.notes: No repayment. Parents or guardians must never have owned a home. Under $20,000 in liquid assets. Stacks with ASSIST for $25,000–$30,000 total; first come, first served.

programs.name: Home Advantage DPA
programs.amountText: 3%, 4% or 5% of loan (5% on FHA or conventional)
programs.notes: 0% deferred second with a Home Advantage first mortgage; no needs assessment for the 3–5% options.

programs.name: Home Advantage Needs Based
programs.notes: 1% interest, payments deferred 30 years.

programs.name: Opportunity DPA
programs.notes: 1% interest, payments deferred 30 years.

programs.name: Veterans DPA
programs.notes: Washington veterans; 3% deferred.

programs.name: Covenant Homeownership Program
programs.amountText: 0% loan covering down payment and closing costs — amount set by program
programs.notes: For first-time buyers whose family lived in Washington before 1968 and was in a group harmed by housing discrimination (per the state’s Covenant study). Repaid at sale or transfer; may be forgiven after 5 years if income was ≤80% AMI. Oversubscribed at times.

programs.name: Easy Close DPA
programs.notes: Repaid monthly alongside the WHEDA Advantage first mortgage. Not limited to first-time buyers.

programs.name: Capital Access DPA
programs.notes: 0% deferred, due when the first mortgage is paid off or refinanced. For lower-income buyers in high-housing-need areas. Available again on a limited basis since Jan 15, 2026.

Madison.name: Home-Buy the American Dream
Madison.notes: Repaid with a share of appreciation at sale.

programs.name: Low Down Home Loan
programs.notes: 2% fixed, repaid over 15 years. Only with the Fund’s Homeownership (mostly first-time) or Movin’ Up programs; full $12,000 when loan-to-value is 80% or higher.

programs.name: Home$tretch DPA
programs.notes: 0% loan, no monthly payments; due at sale, refinance or after 30 years. Pairs with the WCDA Standard First-Time Homebuyer loan.

programs.name: Amortizing DPA
programs.notes: Low-rate loan with up to a 120-month term; pairs with WCDA Advantage (no first-time requirement).
